## Order-to-cash

Use these tables for questions about order-to-cash. Written by Krusgraph by rules from the plan and validate_plan's counts. A person approves this text by reading create_data_agent's dry run and calling it again with dry_run=false; Krusgraph writes nothing before that.

### Tables and what their fields mean

- `sap.sap_t001` (T001: Company codes): one row per MANDT + BUKRS (key rule SAP pack).
  - `MANDT`: part of the key.
  - `BUKRS`: part of the key.
- `sap.sap_tvko` (TVKO: Sales organizations): one row per MANDT + VKORG (key rule SAP pack).
  - `MANDT`: part of the key; points at sap_t001.MANDT+BUKRS (rule SAP pack).
  - `VKORG`: part of the key.
  - `BUKRS`: points at sap_t001.MANDT+BUKRS (rule SAP pack).
- `sap.sap_mara` (MARA: Material master, general data): one row per MANDT + MATNR (key rule SAP pack). MATNR is 18 characters in ECC and 40 in S/4HANA; numeric material numbers are stored with leading zeros.
  - `MANDT`: part of the key.
  - `MATNR`: part of the key.
- `sap.sap_makt` (MAKT: Material descriptions): one row per MANDT + MATNR + SPRAS (key rule SAP pack). One row per material and language: filter on SPRAS before joining, or every order line is repeated once per language.
  - `MANDT`: part of the key; points at sap_mara.MANDT+MATNR (rule SAP pack).
  - `MATNR`: part of the key; points at sap_mara.MANDT+MATNR (rule SAP pack).
  - `SPRAS`: part of the key.
- `sap.sap_vbak` (VBAK: Sales document, header): one row per MANDT + VBELN (key rule SAP pack). Orders, quotations, contracts and returns share this table; AUART (and VBTYP) tell them apart.
  - `MANDT`: part of the key; points at sap_kna1.MANDT+KUNNR (rule SAP pack); points at sap_tvko.MANDT+VKORG (rule SAP pack).
  - `VBELN`: part of the key.
  - `KUNNR`: points at sap_kna1.MANDT+KUNNR (rule SAP pack).
  - `VKORG`: points at sap_tvko.MANDT+VKORG (rule SAP pack).
  - `NETWR`: an amount at header level, in the currency of WAERK.
  - `ERDAT`: a date the pack lists for changes (delta).
  - `AEDAT`: a date the pack lists for changes (delta).

  - `MATNR`: points at sap_mara.MANDT+MATNR (rule SAP pack).
  - `AUBEL`: points at sap_vbap.MANDT+VBELN+POSNR (rule SAP pack).

  - `VGPOS`: points at sap_lips.MANDT+VBELN+POSNR (rule SAP pack).

- `sap.sap_vbfa` (VBFA: Sales document flow): one row per MANDT + VBELV + POSNV + VBELN + POSNN + VBTYP_N (key rule SAP pack). A link table between any preceding and any subsequent document: an order item can have several deliveries and a delivery can serve several orders. VBTYP_V and VBTYP_N say which kind of document each side is.
  - `MANDT`: part of the key.
  - `VBELV`: part of the key.
  - `POSNV`: part of the key.
  - `VBELN`: part of the key.
  - `POSNN`: part of the key.
  - `VBTYP_N`: part of the key.

- `sap_makt.MANDT = sap_mara.MANDT AND sap_makt.MATNR = sap_mara.MATNR`: sap_makt to sap_mara, many-to-one (rule SAP pack; counted: 6 of 6 rows with a value find their sap_mara row (100.0% match); the target key is unique).
- `sap_tvko.MANDT = sap_t001.MANDT AND sap_tvko.BUKRS = sap_t001.BUKRS`: sap_tvko to sap_t001, many-to-one (rule SAP pack; counted: 2 of 2 rows with a value find their sap_t001 row (100.0% match); the target key is unique).
- `sap_lips.MANDT = sap_likp.MANDT AND sap_lips.VBELN = sap_likp.VBELN`: sap_lips to sap_likp, many-to-one (rule SAP pack; counted: 2 of 2 rows with a value find their sap_likp row (100.0% match); the target key is unique).
- `sap_lips.MANDT = sap_vbap.MANDT AND sap_lips.VGBEL = sap_vbap.VBELN AND sap_lips.VGPOS = sap_vbap.POSNR`: sap_lips to sap_vbap, many-to-one (rule SAP pack; counted: 2 of 2 rows with a value find their sap_vbap row (100.0% match); the target key is unique).
- `sap_lips.MANDT = sap_mara.MANDT AND sap_lips.MATNR = sap_mara.MATNR`: sap_lips to sap_mara, many-to-one (rule SAP pack; counted: 2 of 2 rows with a value find their sap_mara row (100.0% match); the target key is unique).
- `sap_likp.MANDT = sap_kna1.MANDT AND sap_likp.KUNNR = sap_kna1.KUNNR`: sap_likp to sap_kna1, many-to-one (rule SAP pack; counted: 1 of 1 rows with a value find their sap_kna1 row (100.0% match); the target key is unique).
- `sap_likp.MANDT = sap_kna1.MANDT AND sap_likp.KUNAG = sap_kna1.KUNNR`: sap_likp to sap_kna1, many-to-one (rule SAP pack; counted: 1 of 1 rows with a value find their sap_kna1 row (100.0% match); the target key is unique).
- `sap_vbrp.MANDT = sap_vbrk.MANDT AND sap_vbrp.VBELN = sap_vbrk.VBELN`: sap_vbrp to sap_vbrk, many-to-one (rule SAP pack; counted: 2 of 2 rows with a value find their sap_vbrk row (100.0% match); the target key is unique).

- `sap_t001.MANDT = sap_adrc.CLIENT AND sap_t001.ADRNR = sap_adrc.ADDRNUMBER` (rule SAP pack): not a key join (valid_on): it needs the pack's extra condition and can match more than one row; not used in the examples.
- `sap_vbfa.MANDT = sap_vbap.MANDT AND sap_vbfa.VBELV = sap_vbap.VBELN AND sap_vbfa.POSNV = sap_vbap.POSNR` (rule SAP pack): not a key join (key): it needs the pack's extra condition and can match more than one row; not used in the examples.
- `sap_vbfa.MANDT = sap_lips.MANDT AND sap_vbfa.VBELN = sap_lips.VBELN AND sap_vbfa.POSNN = sap_lips.POSNR` (rule SAP pack): not a key join (key): it needs the pack's extra condition and can match more than one row; not used in the examples.
- `sap_vbfa.MANDT = sap_vbrp.MANDT AND sap_vbfa.VBELN = sap_vbrp.VBELN AND sap_vbfa.POSNN = sap_vbrp.POSNR` (rule SAP pack): not a key join (key): it needs the pack's extra condition and can match more than one row; not used in the examples.
- `sap_vbfa.MANDT = sap_vbak.MANDT AND sap_vbfa.VBELN = sap_vbak.VBELN` (rule SAP pack): not a key join (key): it needs the pack's extra condition and can match more than one row; not used in the examples.

- `sap_vbfa.MANDT = sap_vbrk.MANDT AND sap_vbfa.VBELN = sap_vbrk.VBELN` (rule SAP pack): not a key join (key): it needs the pack's extra condition and can match more than one row; not used in the examples.

### Known traps

- sap_vbak.NETWR is one value per sap_vbak row; a join with sap_vbap repeats it on every sap_vbap row. Never SUM(sap_vbak.NETWR) over sap_vbap rows: sum it on sap_vbak first (one row per sap_vbak) and join the result.
- sap_vbap.NETWR is one value per sap_vbap row; a join with sap_vbep repeats it on every sap_vbep row. Never SUM(sap_vbap.NETWR) over sap_vbep rows: sum it on sap_vbap first (one row per sap_vbap) and join the result.
- sap_vbap.NETWR is one value per sap_vbap row; a join with sap_lips repeats it on every sap_lips row. Never SUM(sap_vbap.NETWR) over sap_lips rows: sum it on sap_vbap first (one row per sap_vbap) and join the result.
- sap_vbrk.NETWR is one value per sap_vbrk row; a join with sap_vbrp repeats it on every sap_vbrp row. Never SUM(sap_vbrk.NETWR) over sap_vbrp rows: sum it on sap_vbrk first (one row per sap_vbrk) and join the result.
- sap_vbrk.MWSBK is one value per sap_vbrk row; a join with sap_vbrp repeats it on every sap_vbrp row. Never SUM(sap_vbrk.MWSBK) over sap_vbrp rows: sum it on sap_vbrk first (one row per sap_vbrk) and join the result.
- sap_vbap.NETWR is one value per sap_vbap row; a join with sap_vbrp repeats it on every sap_vbrp row. Never SUM(sap_vbap.NETWR) over sap_vbrp rows: sum it on sap_vbap first (one row per sap_vbap) and join the result.
- Two views over the same rows: I_SalesOrder and I_SalesDocument read the same header table (VBAK), I_SalesOrder only the orders; I_SalesOrderItem and I_SalesDocumentItem the same items (VBAP). A lakehouse that lands both, or a view next to the table it reads, holds every order twice: adding their amounts together doubles the total. The pack lists what each view corresponds to (corresponds_to) so a person can see it; it does not join a view to its table.
- An account number needs its chart of accounts: SAKNR is unique only within a chart of accounts (KTOPL), and SKB1 and journal lines carry no KTOPL: it comes from the company code, T001.KTOPL. Join SKA1 (for the account's name) through T001, not on SAKNR alone.
- Header amounts and item amounts are different levels: VBAK.NETWR is the net value of the whole document, VBAP.NETWR that of one item. Summing VBAK.NETWR over a join with VBAP counts each order once per item (Krusgraph's 'the total that doubles' check, amounts.py); summing VBAP.NETWR over a join with VBEP counts each item once per schedule line. Sum each amount on its own table.
- Currency per document: NETWR is in the document currency WAERK, which can differ from document to document. Adding NETWR across documents without converting adds different currencies. VBRP has no currency of its own; its amounts are in VBRK.WAERK.
- VBFA is many-to-many: An order item can be delivered in several deliveries and a delivery can serve several orders; the same holds between deliveries and invoices. VBFA records each pair. Joining orders to invoices through VBFA multiplies rows on both sides: aggregate on one side first, and filter VBTYP_V/VBTYP_N to the document kinds you mean.
- Sold-to, ship-to and payer may differ: VBAK.KUNNR is the sold-to party. The ship-to party and the payer are rows of VBPA (PARVW), and on deliveries and billing documents in LIKP.KUNNR and VBRK.KUNRG. 'Revenue per customer' needs a choice of which of them.
- Text tables have one row per language: MAKT has one row per material and language; filter SPRAS before joining.
- Documents find their conditions through KNUMV: VBAK, VBRK and EKKO carry a condition number KNUMV; their conditions are the KONV (ECC) or PRCD_ELEMENTS (S/4HANA) rows with that KNUMV, and an item's are those with KPOSN equal to the item number. Joining on the document number VBELN or EBELN finds nothing.

name: Customer master
description: "Questions about customer master: ADR6 E-mail addresses of addresses; ADRC Addresses (central address management); KNA1 Customer master, general data; KNVK Contact persons; VBPA Partners of sales, delivery and billing documents"
---

## Customer master

Use these tables for questions about customer master. Written by Krusgraph by rules from the plan and validate_plan's counts. A person approves this text by reading create_data_agent's dry run and calling it again with dry_run=false; Krusgraph writes nothing before that.

### Tables and what their fields mean

- `sap.sap_kna1` (KNA1: Customer master, general data): one row per MANDT + KUNNR (key rule SAP pack). In S/4HANA customers are maintained as business partners; KNA1 is still the customer table that sales documents point at.
  - `MANDT`: part of the key.
  - `KUNNR`: part of the key.
  - Left out as personal data by name: NAME1, STRAS, PSTLZ, ORT01, TELF1. Do not select, group by or show them.
- `sap.sap_vbpa` (VBPA: Partners of sales, delivery and billing documents): one row per MANDT + VBELN + POSNR + PARVW (key rule SAP pack). One row per document, item and partner function. POSNR 000000 holds the partners of the whole document. PARVW is the internal function code (AG sold-to, WE ship-to, RE bill-to, RG payer; shown as SP, SH, BP, PY in English logons). Sold-to, ship-to and payer may be three different customers.
  - `MANDT`: part of the key; points at sap_kna1.MANDT+KUNNR (rule SAP pack); points at sap_knvk.MANDT+PARNR (rule SAP pack).
  - `VBELN`: part of the key.
  - `POSNR`: part of the key.
  - `PARVW`: part of the key.
  - `KUNNR`: points at sap_kna1.MANDT+KUNNR (rule SAP pack).
  - `PARNR`: points at sap_knvk.MANDT+PARNR (rule SAP pack).
- `sap.sap_knvk` (KNVK: Contact persons): one row per MANDT + PARNR (key rule SAP pack). One row per contact person of a customer (KUNNR) or a supplier (LIFNR); NAMEV is the first name, NAME1 the last name. Every row is about a person.
  - `MANDT`: part of the key; points at sap_kna1.MANDT+KUNNR (rule SAP pack).
  - `PARNR`: part of the key.
  - `KUNNR`: points at sap_kna1.MANDT+KUNNR (rule SAP pack).
  - Left out as personal data by name: NAMEV, NAME1, TELF1. Do not select, group by or show them.
- `sap.sap_adrc` (ADRC: Addresses (central address management)): one row per CLIENT + ADDRNUMBER + DATE_FROM + NATION (key rule SAP pack). Shared by customers, suppliers, company codes, business partners and document partners, through an address number. The key also has the start of validity (DATE_FROM) and the version (NATION: blank for the standard version, other values for the same address in another script, such as Latin and Kanji).
  - `CLIENT`: part of the key.
  - `ADDRNUMBER`: part of the key.
  - `DATE_FROM`: part of the key.
  - `NATION`: part of the key.
  - Left out as personal data by name: NAME1, STREET, POST_CODE1, CITY1. Do not select, group by or show them.
- `sap.sap_adr6` (ADR6: E-mail addresses of addresses): one row per CLIENT + ADDRNUMBER + PERSNUMBER + DATE_FROM + CONSNUMBER (key rule SAP pack). Several e-mail addresses per address and person, like ADR2. FLGDEFAULT marks the standard one.
  - `CLIENT`: part of the key.
  - `ADDRNUMBER`: part of the key.
  - `PERSNUMBER`: part of the key.
  - `DATE_FROM`: part of the key.
  - `CONSNUMBER`: part of the key.
  - Left out as personal data by name: SMTP_ADDR. Do not select, group by or show them.

### Checked joins (use these)

- `sap_vbak.MANDT = sap_kna1.MANDT AND sap_vbak.KUNNR = sap_kna1.KUNNR`: sap_vbak to sap_kna1, many-to-one (rule SAP pack; counted: 3 of 3 rows with a value find their sap_kna1 row (100.0% match); the target key is unique).
- `sap_likp.MANDT = sap_kna1.MANDT AND sap_likp.KUNNR = sap_kna1.KUNNR`: sap_likp to sap_kna1, many-to-one (rule SAP pack; counted: 1 of 1 rows with a value find their sap_kna1 row (100.0% match); the target key is unique).
- `sap_likp.MANDT = sap_kna1.MANDT AND sap_likp.KUNAG = sap_kna1.KUNNR`: sap_likp to sap_kna1, many-to-one (rule SAP pack; counted: 1 of 1 rows with a value find their sap_kna1 row (100.0% match); the target key is unique).
- `sap_vbrk.MANDT = sap_kna1.MANDT AND sap_vbrk.KUNAG = sap_kna1.KUNNR`: sap_vbrk to sap_kna1, many-to-one (rule SAP pack; counted: 1 of 1 rows with a value find their sap_kna1 row (100.0% match); the target key is unique).
- `sap_vbrk.MANDT = sap_kna1.MANDT AND sap_vbrk.KUNRG = sap_kna1.KUNNR`: sap_vbrk to sap_kna1, many-to-one (rule SAP pack; counted: 1 of 1 rows with a value find their sap_kna1 row (100.0% match); the target key is unique).
- `sap_vbpa.MANDT = sap_kna1.MANDT AND sap_vbpa.KUNNR = sap_kna1.KUNNR`: sap_vbpa to sap_kna1, many-to-one (rule SAP pack; counted: 4 of 4 rows with a value find their sap_kna1 row (100.0% match); the target key is unique).
- `sap_knvk.MANDT = sap_kna1.MANDT AND sap_knvk.KUNNR = sap_kna1.KUNNR`: sap_knvk to sap_kna1, many-to-one (rule SAP pack; counted: 1 of 1 rows with a value find their sap_kna1 row (100.0% match); the target key is unique).
- `sap_vbpa.MANDT = sap_knvk.MANDT AND sap_vbpa.PARNR = sap_knvk.PARNR`: sap_vbpa to sap_knvk, many-to-one (rule SAP pack; counted: 1 of 1 rows with a value find their sap_knvk row (100.0% match); the target key is unique).

### Joins not to use without asking

- `sap_kna1.MANDT = sap_adrc.CLIENT AND sap_kna1.ADRNR = sap_adrc.ADDRNUMBER` (rule SAP pack): not a key join (valid_on): it needs the pack's extra condition and can match more than one row; not used in the examples.
- `sap_t001.MANDT = sap_adrc.CLIENT AND sap_t001.ADRNR = sap_adrc.ADDRNUMBER` (rule SAP pack): not a key join (valid_on): it needs the pack's extra condition and can match more than one row; not used in the examples.
- `sap_vbpa.MANDT = sap_adrc.CLIENT AND sap_vbpa.ADRNR = sap_adrc.ADDRNUMBER` (rule SAP pack): not a key join (valid_on): it needs the pack's extra condition and can match more than one row; not used in the examples.
- `sap_adr6.CLIENT = sap_adrc.CLIENT AND sap_adr6.ADDRNUMBER = sap_adrc.ADDRNUMBER AND sap_adr6.DATE_FROM = sap_adrc.DATE_FROM` (rule SAP pack): not a key join (key): it needs the pack's extra condition and can match more than one row; not used in the examples.

### Known traps

- The partner number is not the customer number: A business partner and the customer or supplier behind it can have different numbers, depending on how number ranges were set up. Join BUT000 to KNA1 or LFA1 through CVI_CUST_LINK or CVI_VEND_LINK, never on PARTNER = KUNNR.
- CLIENT, not MANDT: The business partner tables call the client column CLIENT. The pack pairs it with MANDT of KNA1 and LFA1 explicitly.
- An address has versions and periods: ADRC's key has the address number, the start of validity and the version (NATION). Joining customers or suppliers to ADRC on the number alone repeats them once per version and period: filter NATION to the standard version and pick the period valid on the date you report for. The pack applies these links that way, for the date of the call (round n28); a report for another date needs that date instead.
- A document can carry its own address: VBPA.ADRNR is filled when an order or delivery has an address of its own for a partner, such as a one-time ship-to address. Where it is empty, the partner's master address (KNA1.ADRNR) applies. Reports of where goods were shipped need the document address first.
- Several numbers and e-mail addresses per address: ADR2 and ADR6 hold one row per number or e-mail address of an address (CONSNUMBER), and per contact person of an organization (PERSNUMBER). A join with them multiplies the address; filter FLGDEFAULT for the standard number, and PERSNUMBER blank for the address itself.
- Names, addresses, numbers and e-mail are personal data: Customers and suppliers can be people, and ADRC, ADR2 and ADR6 hold their names, streets, telephone numbers and e-mail addresses. The pack names these columns, so sample_rows masks them and drafted queries and gold views leave them out, as for any column the privacy rules flag; show_personal_data=true shows them, and the user's own permissions apply either way. SAP's field names (SMTP_ADDR, TELF1, STRAS) say nothing to the general name rules.
- Sold-to, ship-to and payer may differ: VBAK.KUNNR is the sold-to party. The ship-to party and the payer are rows of VBPA (PARVW), and on deliveries and billing documents in LIKP.KUNNR and VBRK.KUNRG. 'Revenue per customer' needs a choice of which of them.
- Contact persons are people, every row: KNVK holds one row per contact person of a customer or supplier: first and last name, telephone, birth date. Unlike KNA1, where a customer may be a company, every KNVK row is about a person. The pack names these columns as personal data, so sample_rows masks them.
